title: Man fatally shot in struggle believed cops would kill him
article: Zoltan Hyacinth predicted he would be killed by police.
The 27-year-old was shot to death by his own gun on March 17 after a struggle with a police officer at a Burger King parking lot in the Keele St. and Wilson Ave. area.
Police had approached Hyacinth's car to apprehend him and his girlfriend who were both suspected in a violent Pizza Pizza robbery on March 14.

"Sadly, Mr. Hyacinth's life foreshadowed his grim demise. In a twist of fate or irony he actually believed that the police would shoot and kill him one day," Hyacinth's lawyer Alonzo Abbey said in a statement.

"In 2007, police tried to arrest Mr. Hyacinth on suspicion that he was carrying a weapon. During that arrest, a Toronto Police Service officer, who believed Mr. Hyacinth was reaching for a weapon, shot at him at close range," Abbey continued. "The shot missed and Mr. Hyacinth fled in fear but was later charged. Those charges were withdrawn but Mr. Hyacinth believed from that day forward that he was a marked man and that he would one day die in an altercation with police officers. It is unclear how exactly Mr. Hyacinth was shot on March 17, 2013 but it seems to be the end he predicted."
According to details released at a recent bail hearing for Hyacinth's girlfriend, Angelica Chaplain, Hyacinth was shot in the head when his gun fired during a struggle with officers.
The Special Investigations Unit, which is probing the incident, has indicated in a statement that no officer shot the man.
A visitation was held on Sunday for Hyacinth at the Ogden Funeral Home at Sheppard Ave. and Brimley Rd where his mother made a brief statement.

"I am grateful to everyone who has shown our family tremendous support during this living nightmare," Michelle Hyacinth said at the funeral home. "It is my hope that everything surrounding Zoltan's death will be transparent to us so we can come to terms with our terrible loss. Zoltan loved life and we loved him. He will be dearly missed."
Hyacinth was killed on a Sunday, but his mother didn't find out until the following Tuesday, said Veronique Henry, another lawyer for Hyacinth.
"She just wants to know what happened to her son, whatever it is," added Henry who had helped represent the dead man in criminal matters.
Henry said the family hasn't decided if they will take any legal action.
